note: Hebrew Aram naharayim ("Aram of the two rivers") is the region of upper Mesopotamia around Haran; the KJV uses the Greek name from the LXX.

kjv: for all the goods of his master were in his hand
mine: with all kinds of his master's good things in his hand
note: The clause vekhol-tuv adonav beyado is circumstantial; it most naturally describes the choice gifts he took along, whereas the KJV "for" makes it a reason (his general authority over the estate).
Hebrew nezem can be an ear or nose ring, but v.47 places it "on her nose" (al-appah), so a nose ring is meant here.
Hebrew ha-almah means a young woman of marriageable age; virginity is stated separately with betulah in v.16. The KJV choice parallels its rendering of almah in Isa 7:14.
Hebrew al-appah means "on her nose" (af, nose); the KJV "face" obscures that the nezem was a nose ring.
